chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ribat, from Abu Sarah, from Hind al-Sarraj, who said:

I said to Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام: “May Allah set you aright. I used to carry weapons to the people of al-Sham and sell them to them. But when Allah made me aware of this matter, I became distressed about that weaponry, and I said: I will not carry it to the enemies of Allah.”
He عليه السلام said: “Carry it to them and sell it to them, for Allah, Exalted is He, repels by means of them our enemy and your enemy,” meaning the Romans.
He عليه السلام said: “So when there is war between us and them, then whoever carries weapons to our enemy which they use to seek aid against us, he is a polytheist.”

key_terms.أَعْدَاءِ اللَّهِ: the enemies of Allah, as understood by the speaker before the Imam's clarification
key_terms.أَهْلِ الشَّامِ: the people of al-Sham, the regional political power mentioned in the report
key_terms.الرُّومَ: the Romans, identified as a common enemy
key_terms.السِّلَاحَ: weapons or arms being transported and sold
key_terms.الْحَرْبُ: a state of warfare that changes the ruling
key_terms.عَدُوِّنَا: our enemy, meaning those fighting against the Imam and his side
key_terms.مُشْرِكٌ: one guilty of shirk, used here as a severe condemnation
key_terms.هَذَا الْأَمْرَ: this matter, referring contextually to recognition of the Imams' cause

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible in Islam to sell weapons to hostile or foreign groups?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal distinction regarding trading arms with political powers. Selling weapons to a group may be permitted when it serves to repel a greater enemy, but supplying arms to those actively at war with the Ahl al-Bayt's side and aiding them against the believers is strictly condemned.
